resources.string: Mind Peace uses Accessibility to notice which app is in front and cover it with a confirmation before you use it. It does not read chats, passwords, or on-screen text — only which app came to the foreground. It runs entirely on your phone and does not collect or upload any usage records.
An ongoing timed session, showing time left.
A reminder when this session ends.

An evening look at today\'s usage versus yesterday.
Mind Peace does not lock your whole phone. When you open a feed or short-video app you tend to get lost in, it covers it with a confirmation and asks if you really want to open it.
Intercept before open, so one swipe doesn\'t take over

When you open a watched app, a confirmation layer appears right away and you can\'t use it yet.
Choose Confirm to continue, or Exit to go home.
Pick a duration (1 / 3 / 5 minutes, or custom).
The timer runs only while this app is in front. Leaving (home, another app) ends the session; leftover time is discarded, and the next open asks again. When time is up you go home and get a reminder.
The system won\'t tell us which app you opened unless you give Mind Peace Accessibility. It is only used to see the foreground app and cover it in time. It will not read your messages.
The countdown needs to keep running quietly. Allow Mind Peace to ignore battery optimization, and allow notifications when the system asks (used to show time left).

The evening recap and “you held off” encouragement both use notifications. The session countdown also shows in a notification. You can finish setup without allowing them now; we\'ll remind you later on the home tab.
We need the list of installed apps so you can choose which ones to watch. Only names and icons are read to build that list. We do not open anything inside those apps.
Some phone makers kill apps in the background, and intercepts stop working. Follow the steps for your phone, then check the box.
Xiaomi / Redmi: in Recents, pull down the Mind Peace card and tap Lock.
Huawei / Honor: lock the card in Recents; allow background running in battery settings.
OPPO / OnePlus: lock from the Recents top-right; allow Mind Peace in autostart.
vivo / iQOO: lock in Recents; allow high background power use.
Pixel / stock Android: ignoring battery optimization is usually enough. No extra lock needed.
I\'ve locked it in Recents (or confirmed it isn\'t needed)

Reading installed apps, receiving notifications, and turning on Accessibility all exist so we can watch the apps you chose more accurately: cover the confirmation layer before they open, let the countdown actually finish, and remind you when it is time. Miss any one of these, and intercepts may fail.

We restate this clearly: Mind Peace never collects privacy data, and never uploads any usage records. It is fully offline. Everything stays on this phone. Accessibility does not read chats, passwords, or on-screen text. It only cares which app has come to the foreground.
If you paid for this app, you were scammed. Mind Peace is free. Anyone who charged you is not us.

string-array.item: Those apps on the list are waiting. You\'re doing just fine without them.
The second your finger stopped, you\'d already won a round.
Those apps are still waiting. You\'ve been living your own day.
This gap isn\'t boredom. It\'s a window you left for yourself.
Not opening them is fine. The world keeps turning, and you\'re clearer.
Today\'s restraint is something tomorrow-you will quietly thank you for.
The urge to scroll came and went. You\'re still here. That\'s good.
The watch list is on duty. You spent the time on something better.
Skip one open, and you get a stretch of your own rhythm back.
The screen can stay on. You didn\'t let it pull you away.
This stretch without those apps is already worth a round of applause.
Attention stood with you today. Rare, and just right.
Those scroll-itch moments passed. You took the day back.
A blank stretch of time, lived as real spare time.
The apps are where you left them. You\'ve already walked a few steps on.
Holding back isn\'t a loss. It\'s you taking the wheel again.
Tonight\'s time is what you picked back out of habit.
You didn\'t slide all the way down. Breathing feels a bit easier.
See? Leave those apps, and the sky doesn\'t fall.
This quiet is yours. Keep it. Don\'t rush to give it back.
